title: REST APIs: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: Picture a restaurant with a menu and a waiter. You order from the menu, and the waiter brings it back. That's how a R E S T A P I works.

scenes.heading: Ordering at the restaurant
scenes.narration: Each H T T P method is a kind of order. GET reads something from the menu. POST creates a new order. PUT replaces an order, and PATCH changes part of it. DELETE cancels it.

scenes.heading: Status codes
scenes.narration: The waiter answers with a number. Two hundred means it worked. Two oh one means something new was created. Four oh one means you're not logged in. And four oh four means it doesn't exist.

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Network devices use it too. One replaces, one modifies. Four oh three means forbidden.

items.wrong: PUT and PATCH are the same

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva REST APIs lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. GET reads, POST creates, PUT replaces, DELETE removes. Two hundred means success. Four oh one is login, and four oh three is forbidden. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva REST APIs lab.
